A digital signature is a mathematical technique used to validate the authenticity and integrity of a digital document. It is the digital equivalent of a handwritten signature or stamped seal, but it offers far more inherent security. How it works: When you generate a digital signature key (PKCS#12 file), the app creates a Public/Private key pair. The Private Key is kept secret by you and used to sign documents. The Public Key is included in a certificate and can be shared with others to verify your signature. What is a P12 file? A .p12 (PKCS#12) file is an archive file format that stores your private key and certificate. It is protected by a password, which you must provide whenever you want to use the key to sign a document. Fields explained: - Alias: A name to identify this key in your storage. - Common Name: Usually your full name. - Organization: The company or entity you belong to. - Country: The two-letter ISO country code (e.g., US, RO, DE).
